title: Blueprint-node split of a stalled lemma into three dependency-chained sub-lemmas
intent: Replace one stalled lemma (`lem:complex`, partial 45/50) by three named blueprint nodes written for it, chained step1 → step2 → step3 → lem:complex by their `uses` fields, each with a reset attempt budget, so work is scheduled from the leaf and the parent's glue is the single `uses` edge to the last child.

parent.name: lem:complex
parent.statement: a complex lemma (schematic; the protocol does not spell out its statement), split into three steps; after the split its `uses` field names `lem:complex_step3` and its attempt budget is reset to 0/50

children.name: lem:complex_step1
children.statement: the first step of the split (schematic; its statement is not spelled out), a leaf node with no `uses` field and a fresh 0/20 budget
children.closed_by: a leaf: its node carries no `uses` field (lines 344-345), so nothing needs to be proved first; its proof closes from its own statement alone

children.name: lem:complex_step2
children.statement: the second step (schematic), whose `uses` field names `lem:complex_step1` and a fresh 0/20 budget
children.closed_by: its `uses` field names `lem:complex_step1` (line 348), the sibling it rests on; it is scheduled only after step1 is done

children.name: lem:complex_step3
children.statement: the third step (schematic), whose `uses` field names `lem:complex_step2` and a fresh 0/20 budget
children.closed_by: its `uses` field names `lem:complex_step2` (line 352); it is the only node the parent cites (line 356), so the parent re-proves from it

applicability.goal_shape: A blueprint node (lemma) whose proof is partial or exhausted and too large or unclear to prove directly; it is replaced by a linear chain of named sub-nodes, each with its own `uses` field and attempt budget, stated before proved.
applicability.use_when: the lemma's attempts are exhausted or its informal proof is unclear — the coordinator's 'Complex' path (lines 134-138) sends it to the Blueprint Agent, which splits it when the proof has 3+ distinct steps; the steps form an ordered dependency chain.
applicability.avoid_when: the lemma is small enough for a single Proof Agent (the 'Simple' path, lines 124-127); the steps are independent rather than chained (then they should be siblings under the parent, not a chain); or the split deepens the dependency graph past the project's depth cap.

claims.claim: The parent node `lem:complex` cites `lem:complex_step3` in its `uses` field — the whole parent glue is that one citation.
The child `lem:complex_step2` cites `lem:complex_step1` in its `uses` field.
The child `lem:complex_step3` cites `lem:complex_step2` in its `uses` field.

The split is a depth-3 chain of three named nodes below the parent: `lem:complex_step1` has no `uses` field (a leaf), `lem:complex_step2` uses `lem:complex_step1` (line 348), `lem:complex_step3` uses `lem:complex_step2` (line 352), and the parent uses `lem:complex_step3` (line 356).
claims.evidence: read of the four `uses` fields in the copied file `prompts/docs/prompts/coordinator.md` lines 344-357: step1 has none, step2 names step1 (348), step3 names step2 (352), parent names step3 (356)

claims.claim: The coordinator's own action list schedules work leaves-first and re-derives the parent from the last child: '2. Select [lem:complex_step1] (no dependencies)' (line 362) and '5. Finally prove original [lem:complex] using step3' (line 365).

metrics.how_counted: glue = the parent node block at lines 355-357 (header, `uses`, status); children = the three node blocks at 344-345, 347-349, 351-353 (a `uses` line adds one line, so the leaf is 2 lines and the chained nodes 3); depth = the `uses` chain parent → step3 → step2 → step1

consequences: The split creates three new nodes, each still `todo` with a fresh attempt budget (0/20), so every child's proof remains to be done; the parent's correctness now rests entirely on the chain holding, and the parent cites only the last child. Obligations: every `uses` edge must stay consistent — a node is eligible only when all its dependencies are done (the selection rule at line 106) — and the parent's `uses` field must name exactly the last child. Failure modes: a child that is not self-contained cannot later close from its own statement; a broken `uses` edge schedules a node before its dependency is proved; and because the parent is re-proved only from step3, a wrong step propagates to the theorem undetected.
